PullRequest.Title: Use attention terminology for agent sessions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace “Input needed” and “Needs input” UI copy with “Attention needed” and “Needs attention”
- use the warning-colored report icon for sessions that need attention
- preserve the existing icon opacity pulse and row background pulse
- update notifications, filters, hovers, settings descriptions, and accessible labels across the editor and Agents window

## Testing

- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted session status, session list, notification, link presentation, and agent session data source tests

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Input needed status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd6a51d9-02cf-4c3f-bfb1-74085dacee18) | ![After: Needs attention status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/beb05d4f-5525-42af-96d7-5bdc51ddf41f) |

## Demo

The demo cycles through Working, Needs Attention, Completed, and Failed in both the editor and Agents window while preserving the existing Needs Attention pulse.

![Agent session states demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eebe322d-89d7-45f7-bdf7-baf14028903e)

Scenarios.Scenario: Session list, session header, comparison rows, chat rows, and collapsed-section indicators render or update a NeedsInput/needs-attention status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An observable status/read/archive change synchronously rerenders the currently bound tree/header template and calls SessionStatusIcon.setStatus; icon selection and DOM replacement are on the UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with rendered templates whose status changes, effectively the visible/virtualized session and chat rows plus visible section headers, not the full stored session collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering is serialized on the UI thread; each template owns one icon widget and its cache key coalesces same-glyph rerenders into a color update.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold status transition creates the icon once. Warm rerenders with the report-icon cache key only recolor the existing element. Template reset/rebinding clears owned DOM and disposables as before; no positive/negative data cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch replaces the seven-element ring spinner, six independent dot animations, and hidden-animation tracking with one codicon span and one existing opacity pulse; cache and virtualization behavior are preserved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact visible row counts and animation compositor behavior vary by window size and platform, but the changed resource direction is unambiguous.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The runtime change reduces DOM nodes, animation count, and tracking work for each visible needs-attention icon; unchanged row-background pulses remain, and the text-only changes do not add render passes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents window session and nested-chat rows render or update a needs-attention status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tree template rendering calls AgentSessionStatusIcon.setStatus synchronously before the visible row is painted.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with visible parent-session and expanded child-chat rows in NeedsInput state after tree virtualization/filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI-thread serialized. Each reusable row template owns one AgentSessionStatusIcon; identical cache keys avoid rebuilding the child icon.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A cold NeedsInput render now creates one codicon span. A warm render only updates its color. Before the diff, the same branch created a six-dot ring spinner and visibility-animation tracker; reset/disposal ownership is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the renderer and CSS show the pre-existing container opacity pulse/background pulse remain while the nested six-dot ring animation is removed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously visible blocked sessions differs by user workload, but no assumption about large lists is needed to establish that per-row work decreases.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change removes nested animation/DOM work and preserves template reuse, reduced-motion handling, and row cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Status labels are produced for filters, hovers, accessibility text, comparison summaries, pickers, voice descriptions, and open-session link presentation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: These synchronous string/switch operations run while their existing UI or presentation object is built; no new prerequisite is added before display.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one label operation per existing rendered item, summary refresh, help invocation, or link presentation; collection scans and render frequency are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: In-process synchronous work follows each owning renderer/event; the diff does not add queues, fan-out, parallelism, or serialization.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Localization and presentation caching behavior are unchanged; only default message literals and one codicon identifier differ.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every traced hunk changes a literal/status icon value without adding a call, loop, allocation over user data, or lifecycle owner.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: string lengths differ slightly, with no changed multiplicity or unbounded payload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The same operations occur at the same cardinality, and the few additional characters are not a realistic CPU, memory, GC, layout, or serialization mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: A session transition emits an OS notification, or a background terminal input detector emits a system steering request
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For session notifications, the existing delayed eligibility/dedupe checks precede host focus/showToast IPC; opening a session remains conditional on a user click. For terminal prompts, the existing output monitor, cancellation checks, duplicate throttle, and active-execution check precede chatService.sendRequest, which is not newly awaited on terminal progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Focus/notify the native host and show an OS toast; optionally open the session after user activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One showToast for each eligible, uncancelled, deduplicated status transition; openSession only after a click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical native calls ran with the previous 'Input needed' body text.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The toast IPC is on notification delivery, not session execution; opening is user-initiated.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe output from an already-running terminal execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing monitor events per active terminal execution, with disposed/cancelled executions suppressed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same terminal was monitored and the same detection event was handled before the label wording changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detection triggers an asynchronous steering notification; terminal execution and monitoring already existed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing system-initiated steering request for a detected terminal prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per distinct detected output, bounded against rapid duplicates by INPUT_NEEDED_NOTIFICATION_THROTTLE_MS; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request with the same terminal output/message/options was sent; only its UI label said 'may need input'.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The promise is not awaited by the event handler and the changed systemInitiatedLabel does not alter request construction or scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One existing toast per eligible deduplicated status transition and one existing steering request per non-duplicate detected terminal prompt within the established throttle behavior; the diff does not change event counts or payload cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Notification scheduling/cancellation and terminal duplicate throttling are unchanged. Existing requests can occur for independent sessions/terminals, but the diff neither increases nor unbounds that concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing notification dedupe keys, cancellation state, focus checks, and terminal last-output/time suppression are unchanged; cold and warm behavior differ only in displayed label text.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced call sites show the changed literals flow into pre-existing calls after unchanged scheduling, dedupe, and throttling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Underlying IPC/network latency is platform/provider dependent, but it is irrelevant to regression magnitude because no boundary placement, count, concurrency, payload scale, or critical-path dependency changed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Expensive boundaries are pre-existing and retain identical frequency, concurrency, and payload shape apart from a constant-size wording change.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 38 changed files and every diff page. The only runtime rendering change replaces needs-attention ring spinners with report codicons, reducing per-visible-row DOM and animation work while retaining existing cache, virtualization, pulse, and disposal behavior. All remaining changes are constant-size labels/tests; traced OS notification, session-open, terminal subprocess-monitoring, and chat-request boundaries are pre-existing and unchanged in cardinality or scheduling. No actionable performance regression was found.
